To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Saddam is not a hero among Sunnis; (2) Saddam's image is not a significant determinant of attitudes toward the insurgency; (3) the insurgency has not yet become a nationalist movement among Sunnis; and (4) the most significant factor associated with positive attitudes toward the insurgency is the belief that Iraqis should have the right to choose their own leaders.

(a) Sunni Iraqis who support Saddam are more likely to be young, male, and religious; (b) they are more likely to feel that their country is being occupied by a foreign power; and (c) they are more supportive of the insurgency.

(1) a majority of Sunnis in Iraq support the insurgency; (2) the level of support is highest among the young, the poor, and those who have a negative attitude toward the presence of the coalition forces; (3) support is lower among those who have a high level of national pride; (4) support is higher among those who have more conservative religious values and among those who are more politically conservative; and (5) there is no significant relationship between social psychological orientation and support
